Rubino.summary: ⓐ The improvement in blood sugar regulation after bariatric surgery is due to the existence of a substance in the body that interferes with the effect of incretin.

c1.text: Bariatric surgery creates a bypass from the stomach directly to the small intestine, improving blood sugar regulation within days rather than as a secondary effect of weight loss.

c2.text: Incretin is secreted by the small intestine when food is consumed and signals the pancreas to secrete insulin, which regulates blood sugar.

c3.text: Ingested food passes sequentially through the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum before entering the large intestine.

c4.text: In mice, bariatric surgery connecting the stomach directly to the jejunum improves blood sugar without reducing body weight or food intake.

c5.text: ⓐ The improvement in blood sugar regulation after bariatric surgery is due to the existence of a substance in the body that interferes with the effect of incretin.

c6.text: Bypassing the duodenum is effective in treating diabetes because it prevents an anti-incretin substance from interfering with incretin.

c7.text: The improvement in blood sugar regulation after bariatric surgery is not due to a substance in the body interfering with incretin.

h1.text: A substance secreted in the duodenum decreases insulin secretion induced by incretin.

h2.text: A substance in the body interferes with the effect of incretin, and bypassing the duodenum prevents its effect.

a.note: Finding an incretin-interfering substance in the duodenum directly supports the anti-incretin hypothesis ⓐ.

h3.text: A surgery where the stomach is removed and the esophagus is directly connected to the duodenum results in improved blood sugar.

h4.text: In this surgery the stomach is removed and food still passes through the duodenum, so the duodenum is not bypassed and the mechanism of ⓐ does not apply.

b.note: The tempting inference that any digestive surgery improving blood sugar supports ⓐ is undercut by h4: the stomach is removed and the duodenum is not bypassed.

h5.text: After Rubino's bariatric surgery, a second surgery reroutes food passing into the jejunum back to the duodenum, and the blood sugar improvement disappears.

h6.text: Rerouting food back to the duodenum restores food contact with the duodenum, which triggers anti-incretin secretion and eliminates the improvement as predicted by ⓐ.

c.note: The naive inference rc1 (disappearance of blood sugar improvement contradicts ⓐ) is undercut by h6 because rerouting food to the duodenum restores anti-incretin secretion as predicted by ⓐ; thus it strengthens rather than weakens ⓐ.
